question: What is the penalty for using the ISI mark without a licence?
answer:
**Short answer**: Using the ISI mark without a licence is punishable with imprisonment for up to one year, or with a fine of not less than one lakh rupees (which may extend up to five times the value of the goods produced, sold, or offered for sale), or with both [1].

**Details**:
- The penalty applies to any person who contravenes the provisions of section 15 of the BIS Act, 2016 [1].
- If the value of the goods or articles produced, sold, or offered for sale cannot be determined, it is presumed that one year's production was in contravention, and the annual turnover of the previous financial year is taken as the value of the goods [1].

question: What does Section 17 of the BIS Act prohibit?
answer:
**Short answer**: Section 17 of the BIS Act prohibits manufacturing, importing, selling, or exhibiting certain notified goods, articles, processes, systems, or services without a valid licence or Standard Mark, applying a Standard Mark without conforming to relevant standards, making false public claims of conformity without a valid certificate or licence, and using a Standard Mark or its colourable imitation without a valid licence [1].

**Details**:
- **Prohibition without licence or Standard Mark**: No person shall manufacture, import, distribute, sell, hire, lease, store, or exhibit for sale any notified goods, article, process, system, or service without a Standard Mark, except under a valid licence [1].
- **Prohibition despite having a licence**: No person shall apply a Standard Mark, even if granted a licence, unless the goods, article, process, system, or service conforms to the relevant standard or prescribed essential requirements [1].
- **Prohibition on false public claims**: No person shall make a public claim through advertisements, sales promotion leaflets, price lists, or make a declaration on goods that they conform to an Indian standard without having a valid certificate of conformity or licence from the Bureau or an approved authority [1].
- **Prohibition on unauthorised use of Standard Mark**: No person shall use or apply a Standard Mark or any colourable imitation thereof in the manufacture, distribution, sale, hire, lease, exhibition, patent title, trademark, or design except under a valid licence from the Bureau [1].

question: Can a BIS officer search premises and seize goods that bear a fake standard mark?
answer:
**Short answer**: Yes, a certification officer appointed by the Bureau may enter and search premises, and seize goods, articles, materials, or documents if there is reason to believe that a contravention has taken place [1][2][3].

**Details**:
- **Power of Entry and Search**: If a certification officer has reason to believe that goods, articles, processes, systems, or services related to a contravention (such as improper use of the Standard Mark or violations of sections 11, 14, 15, 17, or 26) are secreted in any place, premises, or vehicle, they may enter and search it [1].
- **Seizure**: The certification officer may seize such goods, articles, and other materials and documents that are useful for or relevant to any proceeding under the Act [1][3].
- **Applicable Procedure**: The provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, relating to searches and seizures apply to every search or seizure made under this provision [1].

question: If a company commits an offence under the BIS Act, who is held responsible?
answer:
**Short answer**:
When a company commits an offence under the BIS Act, every director, manager, secretary, other officer in charge of and responsible to the company for the conduct of its business, any authorized representative, as well as the company itself, are deemed guilty and liable to be proceeded against and punished [1].

**Details**:
- **Applicability**: This applies regardless of whether the offence was committed with or without the consent, connivance, or neglect of the officers or representatives [1].
- **Definition of Company and Director**: For the purposes of this provision, a "company" means a body corporate and includes a firm or other association of individuals, and a "director" in relation to a firm means a partner in the firm [1].

**Sources:**

question: Can I copy and publish an Indian Standard on my website?
answer:
**Short answer**: No, you cannot publish, reproduce, or record any Indian Standard or part of it without the authorisation of the Bureau [1]. However, individuals are permitted to make a copy of an Indian Standard for personal use [1].

**Details**:
- **Copyright Protection**: The copyright in any Indian Standard or publication of the Bureau vests solely in the Bureau, notwithstanding any other law [1].
- **Prohibition**: Section 11 of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 explicitly prohibits any individual from publishing, reproducing, or recording any Indian Standard, part thereof, or any BIS publication in any manner or form without prior authorisation [1].
- **Misrepresentation**: No person is allowed to issue a document that creates or may create the impression that it is or contains an Indian Standard unless authorised [1].

question: Under which section can the Central Government make BIS certification compulsory for a product?
answer:
**Short answer**: The Central Government can make BIS certification compulsory for a product under Section 16 of the BIS Act, 2016 [1].

This order can direct that goods, articles, processes, systems, or services conform to a standard and make the use of the Standard Mark under a licence or certificate of conformity compulsory [1].

question: Can an offence under the BIS Act be compounded, and what is the limit?
answer:
**Short answer**: Yes, an offence committed for the first time under the BIS Act, 2016, can be compounded by an officer authorized by the Director General, provided it is not punishable with imprisonment only [1][2].

**Details**
Compounding is not a matter of right [1][3]. The compounding authority will consider the application, hear the applicant, and may either allow the application (specifying the amount) or reject it [1]. If the offence is compounded before prosecution is instituted, no prosecution shall be initiated; if it is compounded after prosecution has begun, the court will be notified, and the person shall be discharged [2].

**Step-by-step**
1. Submit an application in Form-‘A’ to the compounding authority [1][4].
2. The compounding authority will request a report from the concerned branch office, which must be furnished within thirty days [1].
4. If allowed, the compounding authority will issue an order indicating the compounding amount [1].
5. The applicant must pay the amount within thirty days of receiving the order and provide proof of payment [5].

**Documents, fees and timelines**
*   **Timelines**: The compounding authority endeavors to decide on the application within sixty days of filing [4]. Payment must be made within thirty days of the order [5].

**What happens if...**
*   **Non-payment**: If the compounding amount is not paid within the specified time, the Bureau may cancel the licence or certificate of conformity [5].

**Compounding amounts**
The compounding amount is based on the maximum fine applicable for the specific offence under Section 29 of the Act [1][2]:
*   **Section 29(1)**: 50% of the maximum fine, subject to a minimum of 25% of the applicable fine [6].
*   **Section 29(2)**: 50% of the maximum fine, subject to a minimum of one lakh rupees [6].
*   **Section 29(3)**: 50% of the maximum fine, subject to a minimum of two lakh rupees [6].
*   **Multiple offences**: If multiple offences are committed, the amount is determined based on the offence for which a higher compounding amount is prescribed [1].

question: Can I use the words 'Indian Standard' in my company name without permission?
answer:
**Short answer**: No, you cannot use any name containing the expression "Indian Standard" or any abbreviation thereof without the previous permission of the Bureau, if it is with a view to deceive or likely to deceive the public [1].

**Details**:
- **Restrictions on Names**: No person shall use any name that resembles the Bureau's name or contains the expression "Indian Standard" or its abbreviation without prior permission, with a view to deceive or likely to deceive the public [1].
- **Registering Authority Restrictions**: Notwithstanding any law for the time being in force, registering authorities shall not register any company, firm, body of persons, trade mark, design, or grant a patent that bears a name or mark in contravention of this restriction [1].
- **Referral to Central Government**: If a question arises before a registering authority on whether a name or mark contravenes this restriction, the registering authority may refer the question to the Central Government, whose decision shall be final [1].

**Official links**:
- BIS website: https://www.bis.gov.in

question: How long does BIS take to grant a licence under option 1 and option 2?

**Short answer**: Under Option 1, the process is expected to be completed within 90 days from the date of receipt of the application [1]. Under Option 2, the process is expected to be completed within 30 days from the date of receipt of the application [1].

**Details**
*   **Option 1**: This timeline applies provided that the documentation, assessment of the unit, and conformity of the product are established as satisfactory at the first instance [1].
*   **Option 2**: This timeline applies if the factory visit is satisfactory and the conformance of the sample to the relevant Indian Standard is established at the first instance [1].

**Step-by-step**
1. **Application**: The applicant submits the application and required documents [2].
2. **Assessment**: A factory visit is conducted to assess infrastructure, production, and quality control [2].
3. **Testing**: Samples are drawn for testing [2].
4. **Grant**: Upon satisfactory assessment and confirmation of product conformity, the licence is granted [1][2].

**Documents, fees and timelines**
*   **Timeline (Option 1)**: 90 days [1].
*   **Timeline (Option 2)**: 30 days [1].
*   **All India First Cases**: These are processed within 45 days of submission, subject to minimum testing time requirements [3].

question: My licence validity has already expired. Can I still renew it?
answer:
**Short answer**: Yes, you may be able to renew your expired licence, depending on how much time has passed since its expiry and the status of your licence.

**Details**
*   **Renewal within 90 days**: If your licence expired due to non-submission of the renewal application and requisite fees, you may submit the application along with the requisite fee and a late fee of ₹ 5,000 within 90 days from the date of validity [1][2].
*   **Dormant Licences**: If you requested to keep your licence in abeyance (dormant) for up to one year, you may apply for renewal within that specified period [3].
*   **Re-application**: If your licence has expired due to non-submission of fees or voluntary surrender, you have the option to re-apply for a fresh grant of licence within one year of expiry with the same scope based on simpler criteria [3][1].
*   **Suspended Licences**: If your licence was under suspension at the time of expiry, the decision to renew may be deferred for up to 180 days from the date of validity to allow for the revocation of suspension [2]. If the suspension is not revoked within this period, the licence shall stand expired [2].

**Step-by-step**
1. Check the current status of your licence on the BIS CARE app [BIS CARE app].
2. If within the 90-day window, apply for renewal through the Manak Online portal, ensuring you include the late fee of ₹ 5,000 [1].
3. If your licence is expired, you may be eligible to re-apply for a fresh grant of licence within one year of expiry [4].
4. Ensure all pending dues, production details, and self-compliance reports are submitted as required [5].

**What happens if...**
*   **Failure to renew within 90 days**: If the renewal application and fees are not received within 90 days of validity, the licence shall stand expired [1][2].
*   **Illegal marking**: You have no right to mark or dispatch products with the Standard Mark after the date of validity [1]. Doing so is a violation of the BIS Act, 2016 [5].
*   **Non-compliance**: Any non-compliance regarding fees or production details may lead to suspension or cancellation proceedings [5].

question: How do I add a new variety or size to my existing ISI licence?
answer:
**Short answer**: You can add a new variety or size to your existing ISI licence by applying for a change in the scope of licence (CSoL) through Form-XIV along with the requisite fee and documents [1].

**Details**:
- One BIS licence is granted for one product and one Indian Standard, but it may cover multiple varieties, grades, or sizes [1].
- To add new varieties, the change must be made with reference to the relevant standard and guidelines [1].
- Fees: An amount of rupees five thousand is chargeable per variety or per group of varieties (where grouping guidelines are available) [2].

**Step-by-step**:
1. Visit the online portal and check the guidelines for Change in Scope of Licence [1].
2. Fill out application Form-XIV for inclusion of new varieties and attach test reports (if applicable) and other required documents [2][3].
3. Pay the requisite fee of ₹5,000 per variety or group of varieties [2].
4. Submit declarations regarding any changes in manufacturing machinery or test equipment in Form-I and Form-II, along with test reports/certificates for additional raw materials or components as required by the applicable option [2].
5. Upon evaluation and satisfactory verification by the Bureau, an endorsement is issued to the licensee in Form-XV [2][4].

**Documents, fees and timelines**:
- **Documents**: Application in Form-XIV, declarations in Form-I and Form-II (if applicable), test reports/certificates of additional raw materials or components, and third-party laboratory test reports (if required under option 2 or when there are changes in infrastructure/sampling groups) [2][3].
- **Fees**: ₹5,000 per variety or per group of varieties [2].

**What happens if...**:
- **Deficiencies**: If any deficiencies are observed in the application, they will be communicated to the firm to provide information within 21 days [5]. If the reply is not received within 21 days or is incomplete, it will be treated as a rejection notice [5].
- **Rejection**: If the application for change in scope is rejected based on the merit of the case, it will be communicated to the licensee [5].

question: What are the reasons for which BIS can reject a licence application?
answer:
**Short answer**: BIS can reject a licence application for reasons such as failure to offer samples for testing within 30 days, repeated sample test failures, lack of required testing facilities or technical personnel, non-payment of financial dues, document tampering, or unethical practices [1].

**Details**:
- **Testing and Samples**: Applications can be rejected if samples are not offered within 30 days of recording the application, or if independent sample testing fails for the second time (including counter sample requests) [1].

**Step-by-step**:
1. If grounds for rejection arise, the Bureau issues a rejection notice providing a minimum of 21 days for the applicant to reply [1].
2. The applicant is given a reasonable opportunity to be heard in person or through an authorized representative [2].
3. If the facts or explanation furnished by the applicant are not satisfactory, the application is rejected [1].
4. The competent authority passes a speaking order for the decision, and the closure of the application is communicated to the applicant [3].

**Documents, fees and timelines**:
- **Timelines**: The applicant must send a reply or seek a hearing within 21 days of the issue of the rejection notice letter [4].
- **Future applications**: Applicants whose cases are rejected may apply afresh with applicable fees as and when they are in a position to comply with requirements [5].

- BIS website: https://www.bis.gov.in

question: What happens if my product fails in testing after I get the licence?
answer:
**Short answer**: If a sample of your product fails in testing after your licence is granted, your licence will be put under immediate suspension, and you will be required to take corrective actions and offer a fresh sample [1].

**Details**:
- **Notice and Suspension**: Upon receipt of a test report showing non-conformity, or upon consecutive/repeated failures, a notice of suspension will be issued or suspension will be imposed immediately [2].
- **Corrective Actions**: You must investigate the reasons for non-conformity, implement corrective actions, retest available stock, and make efforts to recall potentially non-conforming products from the market [2][3].
- **Revocation of Suspension (RoS)**: Revocation of suspension is considered based on conforming test reports of fresh samples from a Third-Party Laboratory (TPL), or through factory testing/undertakings depending on whether you have an in-house test facility and the specific testing requirements [4][5][1].

**Step-by-step**:
1. Receive the suspension notice or intimation of sample failure from BIS [5].
2. Investigate the root cause, implement corrective actions, and retest your available stock [6].
3. Inform BIS of the corrective actions taken and confirm your readiness to offer fresh samples produced under the improved process [1].
4. BIS will organize an inspection visit (normally within 15 days of receiving a complete reply) to verify corrective actions and draw a fresh sample for testing [5].
5. If the fresh sample shows conformity and corrective actions are satisfactory, the suspension may be revoked (RoS) [4].

**What happens if...**:
- **Fresh sample fails again or no sample is offered**: If the fresh sample tested in a TPL or FT shows non-conformity again, or if you fail to offer a fresh sample and inform corrective actions within 30 days of suspension, proceedings for the cancellation of your licence shall be initiated [4][1].

question: Can small (MSME) manufacturers use shared testing facilities instead of their own lab?
answer:
**Short answer**: Yes, MSME manufacturers can utilise shared testing facilities such as Cluster Based Test Facilities (CBTFs) or other alternative testing arrangements to comply with quality control requirements under Scheme-I [1][2][3].

**Details**:
- **Cluster Based Test Facilities (CBTFs)**: Established to support micro, small, and medium enterprises that may face practical problems in setting up full in-house test facilities due to initial capital requirements, recurring costs, and development time [1]. CBTFs can be located outside the premises of any manufacturer (such as those set up by industry associations, government institutions, or entrepreneurs) or within the premises of a manufacturer [4].
- **Scope and Exceptions**: While CBTFs can be treated as an in-house test facility for operating the Scheme of Testing and Inspection (SIT), certain checks cannot be shifted to a CBTF and must be handled in-house:
  - Tolerances of size and geometry (e.g., dimensions, shape in the form of flatness, straightness, etc.) [5].
  - Visual examination up to 10x magnification level [5].
  - Workmanship like absence of burrs, solder flux splatter, sharp edges, etc [5].
  - Any requirement which necessitates quality checks during the production process [5].

**Step-by-step**:
1. The manufacturer must submit a request to the concerned Branch Office (BO) to consider the CBTF as their in-house test facility along with the required undertaking [6][7].
2. The concerned BO arranges a visit to verify the availability, working condition, and testing capacity of the CBTF vis-à-vis the number of manufacturers utilizing it [6][7].
3. Upon a successful assessment of adequacy, the request for utilisation of the CBTF is accepted [7].
4. During the operation of the licence, the manufacturer maintains proper in-house records as per the SIT and makes proper arrangements for sample handling and identification [8].

**Documents, fees and timelines**:
- **Documents**: An undertaking as per Annexure-X (or as specified in the guidelines) must be submitted by the manufacturer desirous of utilising a CBTF [6][8].
- **Fees**: Special Inspection Charges for any extra day(s) required for the visit and verification of the CBTF shall be borne by the manufacturer [7][6]. Any arrangements or travel expenses resulting from moving from the manufacturing premises to the CBTF for BIS inspection and testing purposes are also borne by the manufacturer [7].

**What happens if...**:
- **Difficulties in utilisation**: If there are any issues or difficulties in the utilisation of a CBTF during the applicant stage, it must be informed to BIS immediately, and the application for grant of licence may be kept on hold [9]. During the operation of the licence, the licensee manufacturer must communicate any difficulties to BIS immediately and on its own suspend the use of the Standard Mark under intimation to BIS [9][6].
- **Suspension due to testing infrastructure**: If a CBTF located within the premises of a manufacturer (illustration type 3(i)(b)) faces licence suspension due to reasons attributable to testing infrastructure (test facility and/or quality control personnel), the licences of other manufacturers using the services of that CBTF shall also be put under suspension [9].

question: What are the main steps to get started with BIS for a new business?
answer:
**Short answer**: To get started with a BIS product certification licence (Scheme-I) for a new business, you must submit an online application with required documents, ensure your manufacturing infrastructure and testing capabilities meet Indian Standards, and undergo a preliminary inspection by BIS [1][2].

**Details**:
- **Essential requirements**: The manufacturer must possess requisite manufacturing infrastructure, appropriate process controls, quality control, and testing capabilities as per the relevant Indian Standard [2].
- **Processing options**: Applications are generally processed under Option-1 or Option-2, depending on product categorization and laboratory availability [3].

**Step-by-step**:
1. Identify the correct Indian Standard (ISS) for your product using the ManakOnline portal [4].
4. Facilitate the preliminary inspection visit by BIS officers to assess your manufacturing infrastructure, process controls, and testing capabilities [2].
5. Provide product samples for testing (either tested during the factory visit, through third-party BIS-recognized laboratories, or a combination) [2].
6. Upon successful evaluation and depositing the annual licence and marking fees, BIS will grant the licence [1].

**Documents, fees and timelines**:
- **Documents**: Application in Form-V, self-evaluation cum verification report (Annexure-I), and relevant technical/factory documents [2].
- **Fees**: Application fee of ₹1,000; inspection fee of ₹7,000 per man day before the preliminary inspection; annual licence fee of ₹1,000 plus the product-specific minimum marking fee upon grant [5].
- **Timelines**: Average time for grant of licence is generally 30 days under Option-2 and 4 months (90 days under standard review) under Option-1 from the date of receipt of a complete application and its recording [6].

**What happens if...**:
- **Deficiencies or non-conformities**: If samples fail testing, corrective actions are required, and the licence may face suspension or cancellation depending on the stage and guidelines [7].
- **Rejection**: Applications may be rejected if samples are not offered within 30 days of recording, if samples fail repeatedly, due to lack of testing facilities or technical personnel, or for tampering with documents, after providing a notice of not less than 21 days [8].

**Short answer**: To update your business name or address (shifting of the manufacturing unit) on a BIS licence, you must submit the required details and documents to BIS, stop using the Standard Mark until the new premises are inspected and found satisfactory, and obtain an endorsement in your licence [1].

**Details**:
- **Change of business name**: For a change in the name of the firm, the change is duly endorsed in the licence as per Annexure-V, and the name of the licensee in the schedule of the licence is changed accordingly [2][3].

- **Use of Standard Mark during relocation**: You must, on your own, stop using the Standard Mark under intimation to the Bureau upon relocating your manufacturing unit to new premises [4]. The use of the Standard Mark can only resume after the new premises are inspected and found to be satisfactory by BIS regarding manufacturing and testing facilities, and the address of the new premises is formally endorsed in the licence [1][4].
- **Revocation of suspension**: The Bureau may do the revocation of suspension after verification of the old premises and verification of the production process at the new premises in accordance with the provisions of paragraph 11 (3) & (4) of Scheme-I of the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018 [5].

question: If BIS raises objections on my application, how much time do I get and what happens next?
answer:
**Short answer**: If BIS raises objections or issues a rejection notice on your application, you are given up to 21 days to send your reply or seek a personal hearing [1][2]. If no reply is received within the stipulated period, the application is processed for rejection without further notice [2].

**Step-by-step**:
1. **Notice period**: You will receive a notice giving you not less than 21 days to submit your written explanation or request a personal hearing (either in person or through an authorised representative) [3].
2. **Review**: The facts or explanations furnished by you are evaluated by the Bureau [4].
3. **Decision**: If the explanation is not satisfactory, or if no reply is received within the stipulated period, the application is processed for rejection as per sub-regulation (6) of regulation 4 of the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018 [1].
4. **Communication**: The closing or rejection of the application is formally communicated to you, after which you may apply afresh with the applicable fee when you are in a position to comply with the requirements [5].

**Documents, fees and timelines**:
- Timeline: A minimum of 21 days from the issue of the notice to respond [3].
- Re-application: If rejected, you may apply afresh with the applicable fee in the future [5].

question: हॉलमार्किंग क्या है और HUID कैसे चेक करें?
answer:

हॉलमार्किंग कीमती धातु के लेखों में कीमती धातु की आनुपातिक सामग्री का सटीक निर्धारण और आधिकारिक रिकॉर्डिंग है [1]। HUID (हॉलमार्क यूनिक आइडेंटिफिकेशन) छह अंकों का एक अल्फ्यूमेरिक नंबर है जो प्रत्येक हॉलमार्क किए गए आइटम के लिए अद्वितीय है, और ग्राहक BIS केयर ऐप में 'Verify HUID' सुविधा का उपयोग करके इसकी जांच कर सकते हैं [2]।

**Details**:
- हॉलमार्किंग योजना का उद्देश्य उपभोक्ताओं को सोने या चांदी से संबंधित शुद्धता में धोखाधड़ी से बचाना, भारत को दुनिया का एक अग्रणी स्वर्ण बाजार केंद्र बनाना और निर्यात प्रतिस्पर्धात्मकता विकसित करना है [2]।

question: लाइसेंस का नवीनीकरण कैसे करें?
answer:
**Short answer**: लाइसेंस का नवीनीकरण (Renewal of Licence) कराने के लिए, लाइसेंसधारी को निर्धारित फॉर्म (Form-XII) के माध्यम से, प्रासंगिक दस्तावेजों और शुल्क के साथ, BIS पोर्टल पर ऑनलाइन आवेदन करना होता है [1][2]。लाइसेंस की समाप्ति से तीन महीने पहले आवेदन करना चाहिए [3]।

**Details**:
* **समय सीमा**: नवीनीकरण आवेदन वैधता तिथि से पहले प्रस्तुत किया जाना चाहिए [4]। यदि आवेदन वैधता के भीतर नहीं मिलता है, तो नवीनीकरण का निर्णय 90 दिनों तक के लिए टाला (defer) जा सकता है [1][4]। वैधता समाप्त होने के 90 दिनों के भीतर विलंब शुल्क के साथ आवेदन किया जा सकता है [1]।
* **उत्पादन विवरण**: वास्तविक आधार पर अंकन शुल्क (marking fee) की गणना के लिए, चार्टर्ड अकाउंटेंट / कॉस्ट अकाउंटेंट द्वारा विधिवत प्रमाणित उत्पादन विवरण प्रस्तुत करना अनिवार्य है [1]।
* **स्व-अनुपालन रिपोर्ट (Self-compliance report)**: नवीनीकरण के समय Annexure-I के अनुसार स्व-अनुपालन रिपोर्ट जमा करना अनिवार्य है [1]।
* **स्वचालित नवीनीकरण (Automatic renewal)**: आवेदन जमा करने के बाद, कुछ अपवादों (जैसे लाइसेंस का निलंबित होना, रद्दीकरण या समाप्ति प्रक्रिया शुरू होना) को छोड़कर, पोर्टल के माध्यम से लाइसेंस स्वतः नवीनीकृत हो जाते हैं [1]।

**Step-by-step**:
1. BIS पोर्टल (Manak Online) पर जाएं [1]।
2. Form-XII में नवीनीकरण आवेदन भरें [1][2]।
3. आवश्यक दस्तावेज और उत्पादन विवरण संलग्न करें [1]।
4. नवीनीकरण आवेदन शुल्क, वार्षिक लाइसेंस शुल्क, अग्रिम न्यूनतम अंकन शुल्क और कोई अन्य बकाया राशि का भुगतान करें [1][2]।
5. स्व-अनुपालन रिपोर्ट (Annexure-I) संलग्न करें [1]।

**Documents, fees and timelines**:
* **शुल्क**: नवीनीकरण आवेदन शुल्क, वार्षिक लाइसेंस शुल्क, और अंकन शुल्क (या न्यूनतम अंकन शुल्क, जो भी अधिक हो) [1][2]। यदि वैधता के 90 दिनों के भीतर आवेदन किया जाता है, तो ₹ 5,000 का अतिरिक्त विलंब शुल्क देना होगा [1]।
* **समय सीमा**: लाइसेंस की समाप्ति से तीन महीने पहले आवेदन करना चाहिए [3]। आवेदन वैधता तिथि से पहले या अधिकतम 90 दिनों के भीतर (विलंब शुल्क के साथ) किया जा सकता है [1][4]।

**What happens if...**:
* यदि 90 दिनों की अवधि के भीतर आवेदन और शुल्क (विलंब शुल्क सहित) प्राप्त नहीं होता है, तो लाइसेंस समाप्त (expire) हो जाएगा [1]।
* यदि लाइसेंस निलंबन (suspension) के अधीन है, तो निलंबन रद्द होने तक नवीनीकरण नहीं किया जाएगा, और निर्णय 180 दिनों तक टाला जा सकता है; यदि इस अवधि में निलंबन रद्द नहीं होता है, तो लाइसेंस समाप्त हो सकता है [1][4]।
